title: Net Metering Rules by State for American Homeowners
excerpt: Understand the net metering laws in your state to make the most of your solar energy system
content:
Section 1: Net Metering Basics

Net metering allows homeowners to generate their own electricity and sell any excess back to the grid. This reduces their energy bills and increases the overall efficiency of their solar energy system.

Section 2: Net Metering by State

Net metering laws vary by state. Some states have favorable policies, while others have more restrictive rules. Check the following list for net metering rules by state: Alabama: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 20 kW. Arizona: Has a maximum system size of 100 kW. California: Has a maximum system size of 5 MW. Colorado: Offers a net metering program for customers of investor-owned utilities. Connecticut: Has a maximum system size of 20 kW. Delaware: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Florida: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. Georgia: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Hawaii: Has a maximum system size of 5 MW. Illinois: Offers a net metering program for customers of investor-owned utilities. Indiana: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 10 kW. Iowa: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Kansas: Has a maximum system size of 1 MW. Kentucky: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Louisiana: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 25 kW. Maine: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Maryland: Has a maximum system size of 2 MW. Massachusetts: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Michigan: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 20 kW. Minnesota: Offers a net metering program for customers of investor-owned utilities. Mississippi: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. Missouri: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Montana: Has a maximum system size of 25 kW. Nebraska: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 100 kW. Nevada: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. New Hampshire: Has a maximum system size of 1 MW. New Jersey: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. New Mexico: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. New York: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. North Carolina: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. North Dakota: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Ohio: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 10 kW. Oklahoma: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Oregon: Has a maximum system size of 2 MW. Pennsylvania: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Rhode Island: Has a maximum system size of 2 MW. South Carolina: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. South Dakota: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Tennessee: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. Texas: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Utah: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 1 MW. Vermont: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Virginia: Has a maximum system size of 2 MW. Washington: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. West Virginia: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 2 MW. Wisconsin: Offers a net metering program for customers of utilities. Wyoming: Allows net metering with a maximum system size of 1 MW.

Conclusion

Visit SolarAtlas to find solar data for your city and check the net metering rules in your state before installing a solar energy system.
